# Overview

`run_cis_qtl_browser()` launches a Shiny application for browsing
`tensorQTL` cis-association results one gene at a time: pick a gene, pick
one of its cis-SNPs, and see the genotype effect plot, the underlying
linear model summary, and a filterable table of every association tested
for that gene. It is the interactive complement to
[`readTQTL()`](tQTLExperiment.html#readtqtl) and
[`plotGenotypeEffect()`](../reference/plotGenotypeEffect.html): rather than
writing `pairs[pairs$gene_name == ...]` by hand for each gene of interest,
the app puts a searchable gene list and SNP dropdown in front of the same
data.

```{r loaddata, message=FALSE}
library(tQTLExperiment)
```

# Inputs

`run_cis_qtl_browser()` needs two things:

- `tqe`: a `tQTLExperiment` with genotype data attached (so it can extract
  phenotype and genotype vectors for the plot and model), and
- `cis_gr`: a `GRanges` of cis-association results, typically the `pairs`
  element returned by `readTQTL(..., mode = "cis_nominal")`, with metadata
  columns identifying the gene, SNP, phenotype, and nominal p-value for
  each row (`gene_col`, `snp_col`, `phenotype_col`, `pval_col` -- their
  defaults match `readTQTL()`'s and `annotateTensorQTLResults()`'s output).

This vignette reuses the pre-computed MAGE chr17 demo results from the
[main vignette](tQTLExperiment.html#demo-data), which need no `tensorQTL`
installation:

```{r demo_load}
cc <- cache_demo_data()
demodir <- dirname(cc$log)

res <- readTQTL(demodir, mode = "cis_nominal")
res$pairs
```

`gene_symbol` is added by `annotateTensorQTLResults()`, which
`run_cis_qtl_browser()`'s default `gene_col` expects:

```{r annotate, eval=FALSE}
newpairs <- annotateTensorQTLResults(res$pairs)
```

For the full `tqe` (genotype-attached) construction used below, see the
main vignette's ["Building a tQTLExperiment"](tQTLExperiment.html#building-a-tqtlexperiment)
section, which builds `tqe` from `CSHLvc2026::mageSEfilt` and the cached
MAGE chr17 PLINK files via `tQTLExperimentFromRSE()`.

# Launching the browser

```{r launch, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("CSHLvc2026")) BiocManager::install("vjcitn/CSHLvc2026")
library(CSHLvc2026)

plink_paths <- cache_mage_chr17_plink()
plpre <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(plink_paths[["bed"]])

data(mageSEfilt, package = "CSHLvc2026")
cd <- as.data.frame(colData(mageSEfilt))
mm <- model.matrix(~ batch + population + sex, data = cd)
mm <- mm[, -1, drop = FALSE]

tqe <- tQTLExperimentFromRSE(
    se              = mageSEfilt,
    plinkPrefix     = plpre,
    covariateMatrix = mm,
    genome          = "hg38"
)
tqe <- addGeneSymbols(tqe)

newpairs <- annotateTensorQTLResults(res$pairs)

# only show associations at pval_nominal <= 0.05
run_cis_qtl_browser(tqe, newpairs, pval_thresh = 0.05)
```

`pval_thresh` is applied once, up front, to `cis_gr` before the app UI is
built -- it is a fixed filter on the whole result set, not an interactive
control in the app itself. Leave it `NULL` (the default) to browse every
tested pair.

# Using the app

The sidebar has:

- **Gene symbol**: a searchable dropdown (`selectizeInput`) over every
  distinct value of `gene_col` in `cis_gr` (after the p-value filter),
- **cis-SNP**: repopulated whenever the gene changes, listing that gene's
  distinct SNPs (from `snp_col`), sorted by nominal p-value,
- **Plot**: an explicit action button -- the genotype-effect plot and
  model summary only (re)render when clicked, not on every dropdown
  change, so that selecting a gene and then a SNP doesn't trigger two
  redraws.

Three tabs share the current gene/SNP selection:

- **Genotype effect**: the beeswarm plot from `plotGenotypeEffect()`,
  phenotype value by genotype (0/1/2 alternate alleles), for the selected
  phenotype-SNP pair.
- **Regression model**: `summary(lm(phenotype ~ genotype + <covariates>))`
  for that same pair, printed verbatim -- the same model
  `qtlRegressionStats()` fits per pair, but shown in full rather than
  reduced to a tidy table. Useful for checking covariate significance or
  residual behavior behind a specific point.
- **cis associations**: a `DT::datatable()` of every row of `cis_gr` for
  the selected gene (ignoring the SNP dropdown), sorted by nominal
  p-value, with per-column filters (`filter = "top"`) for further
  narrowing by hand.
